body:
## What to build

Reject a locally detectable error at the start of a Grouping specification before acquiring typed backend metadata, even when a later independent selection needs column types. Preserve the original selection condition and its precedence without evaluating the later selector.

On main snapshot `339315c387f31deace77566f5d3294b15b323865`, inspect a DuckDB table with one integer column x. A Grouping set selecting absent followed by x fails with the expected missing-column condition and sends no query. Changing only the second selection to a numeric type predicate sends a zero-row input query before the same missing-column condition. A temporary trace of the DBI query method confirmed the invocation; this was not inferred from a Sent query record. The later predicate itself was never evaluated.

On an otherwise supported derived dtplyr input whose types cannot safely be determined without source work, that same change hides the missing-column condition behind the metadata refusal and asks the caller to collect the input. The first error is decidable from the locally available column names, so neither the query nor that remediation is needed. ADR 0005 requires this error to precede backend metadata acquisition.

Closed #342 improved classification of entirely names-only selections. This finding concerns an independently invalid leading selection in a mixed names/type-dependent specification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve the original condition for the demonstrated missing-column and invalid leading-selection expressions before typed metadata acquisition.
- [ ] Cover mixed selections within a Grouping set and across nested grouping families, through inspection and the affected Margin verbs.
- [ ] Prove that the DuckDB failure invokes no input metadata query and that the dtplyr failure reports the original selection error without asking for collection.
- [ ] Do not execute later predicates, force arbitrary caller bindings, or change valid selection evaluation order to perform the preflight.
- [ ] Preserve valid typed selections, the existing metadata/query policy, and lazy construction; add focused public-interface regressions and pass the Package-affecting Review-ready check.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[Dated investigation, minimized reproduction and executable replay evidence](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/1adc767d37bf97288b8a00da16f0ae8cc027c4f8/investigation/summary-grouping-total-share-bughunt-2026-10-31.md#f1-a-typed-sibling-disabled-leading-names-only-error-preflight). Recorded in PR #1098, which contains investigation material only.
title: [P2] Reject leading names-only Grouping errors before typed metadata acquisition

body:
## What to build

Report a locally known overlap between fixed keys and Grouping dimensions before acquiring metadata for an independent later typed selection. ADR 0005 requires locally decidable preparation errors before backend reads.

On main `978d7bef4247bf1348af5b90bfab47924db25500`, fix column a and begin a Grouping specification with a. With a later names-only selection, inspection reports that a cannot appear in both positions. Changing only that later selection to a type predicate causes a live DuckDB zero-row query before the same error. On a derived dtplyr input whose metadata cannot safely be obtained, the overlap is hidden by a metadata refusal recommending collection, although collection cannot make the overlap valid.

A 130-call public matrix covers all five constructors and the shared consumers. All 65 names-only controls report the overlap without metadata queries; typed cases expose 25 replaced dtplyr diagnostics and 15 actual DuckDB DBI invocations. Local typed controls retain the overlap diagnostic.

[Minimal replay, actual-query trace, matrix and causal analysis](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/49e1d16ff42ba33f776e25bc5e895d4296f24371/investigation/2026-11-02-summary-grouping-share-bug-hunt/grouping/README.md). Report mode exits zero and the contract assertion exits one. Tested with R 4.6.1, dtplyr 1.3.3, DuckDB 1.5.5 and dbplyr 2.6.0. Closed #1090 and merged #1120 were read with comments: they repaired invalid selections themselves; this residual failure concerns the plan-level overlap of already resolved values.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reject an already established fixed-key/Grouping-dimension overlap before an independent typed sibling can trigger metadata acquisition.
- [ ] Preserve the overlap diagnostic and caller column spelling on unsafe-metadata dtplyr inputs, and invoke no DuckDB metadata query for the established invalidity.
- [ ] Cover the shared preparation path through inspection and the supported Margin verbs, including the five constructor forms evidenced by the matrix.
- [ ] Retain valid typed selection behavior, existing leading-invalid-selection checks and ordinary selection evaluation semantics.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: [P2] Reject known fixed-key overlaps before typed Grouping metadata

body:
## What to build

Preserve ordinary empty-dots forwarding when fixed-key selectors or Grouping specification constructors receive a valid tidyselect helper argument. A reusable wrapper called without optional columns must resolve an empty selection or report the constructor's documented empty-dimension refusal, rather than failing in an internal classifier.

On main `978d7bef4247bf1348af5b90bfab47924db25500`, a one-row input with one column is enough. Define a wrapper with `...` that calls `inspect_grouping()` using `all_of(c(...))` as `.by`, then call that wrapper with no arguments. It raises `getvarError: argument "value" is missing, with no default` from an internal iterator. Direct tidyselect evaluation in that same wrapper returns an empty selection. Supplying a column name also succeeds. The equivalent selector inside `grouping_set()` fails in the same way, as do both nesting Margin verbs.

The finite matrix compared 360 public calls: 120 empty-dots classifier failures and 240 populated-dots or whole-helper-wrapper controls that succeeded or raised the required empty rollup/cube Package condition. It covered `all_of` and `any_of`, concatenated and unlisted dots, fixed-key position and all five constructors, inspection and all four Margin verbs. Wrapping the whole helper with `identity()` avoided the defective names-only classification. An independent public-seam reproduction confirmed six inspect/nesting failures and their successful populated controls.

The failure was independently reached in the names-only helper-argument reader on the empty `...` symbol, before actual selection resolution. This differs from #1138, whose populated local summary selectors lose their forwarding environment when raw quoted arguments are staged. Full bodies/comments of #1138, #351, #925, #1139 and PR #1142 were checked, along with all-state issue/PR searches; none reported this empty-dots Grouping classifier boundary. The repairs are independently verifiable and neither blocks the other.

Tested with R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, tidyselect 1.2.1 and rlang 1.3.0.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The demonstrated empty-dots fixed-key and constructor selectors agree with direct tidyselect selection through inspection and both nesting verbs, and through the shared expansion/summary consumers.
- [ ] An empty selection yields the correct empty grouping set where allowed; empty rollup/cube dimensions retain their documented Package conditions.
- [ ] Preserve populated forwarding, concatenated/unlisted dots, the successful whole-helper wrapper control, captured environments and ordinary evaluation budgets.
- [ ] Do not force missing dots into a local value or execute caller selectors during static names-only classification merely to discover their selection.
- [ ] Add focused public-seam regression coverage that distinguishes no dots from an explicitly missing argument and from the populated summary-forwarding boundary in #1138.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: [P2] Preserve empty dots forwarding in Grouping selectors

body:
## What to build

Resolve a type-dependent tidy-select expression against the input's typed metadata, even when the outer call is a helper normally driven by column names. Apply the same selection meaning to fixed keys and Grouping specification dimensions.

At main commit `b6f9faba946521aeb92fcf2c5655a2c3bf608ec8`, an input with character `a` = x/y and numeric `b` = 1/1, grouped by an `all_of()` argument that selects numeric columns using `peek_data()`, should have fixed key `b` and one summary row with count two. dplyr returns that result. The Margin summary selects both `a` and `b`, returning two rows with count one. Inspection reports the same wrong fixed keys. In a Grouping specification, the same misclassification can falsely report overlap with a character fixed key.

The name-only preflight treats the leaf helper as conclusive without accounting for its argument's dependence on types. A wrapper around the same selection succeeds, confirming that the typed snapshot itself is usable. This extends the names-alone invariant established in #342 and #346.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The numeric-selection example reports only `b` as fixed and returns one count-two row, matching direct dplyr selection.
- [ ] The equivalent Grouping specification includes `b` without falsely overlapping fixed `a`.
- [ ] Helper arguments whose answers require types reach typed selection; expressions settled by names retain their early-error and query guarantees.
- [ ] Tests cover inspection and the public summary result, including helper and wrapper spellings of the same selection.
- [ ] Existing selection evaluation-count guarantees remain intact.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[2026-10-25 investigation and cause-isolating controls](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/9d10d84095181e07b7db4554608f389a234890c7/investigation/2026-10-25-grouping-summary-bug-hunt/README.md#f2-type-dependent-helper-arguments-used-a-name-only-proxy) include the pinned main baseline, environment, and expected/actual behavior. [Public-contract replay](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/9d10d84095181e07b7db4554608f389a234890c7/investigation/2026-10-25-grouping-summary-bug-hunt/reproduce.R) and [measured baseline output](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/9d10d84095181e07b7db4554608f389a234890c7/investigation/2026-10-25-grouping-summary-bug-hunt/reproduce-output.txt) preserve the executable evidence.
title: [P2] Resolve type-dependent selection-helper arguments against typed metadata

body:
## What to build

Resolve fixed keys and Grouping specification dimensions against the input types when tidyselect evaluates a qualified or parenthesized operator as an ordinary R call. Only expressions whose result or refusal is actually determined by column names may use the names-only pass.

A normal wrapper in the investigation has a default selection argument that chooses the numeric columns from the active tidyselect data. Its input has a character column named like that wrapper argument and a numeric key whose two values are identical. Direct dplyr selects only the numeric key. When the argument is wrapped in qualified base c, inspection selects the character column as well, and both nesting verbs split the two source rows into separate cells rather than one. An explicit caller-promise variant selects the character column instead of the numeric key. No active binding or forged Grouping specification is needed.

The names-only classifier treats qualified and parenthesized operator operands as tidyselect selection syntax, although ordinary call evaluation resolves the operand through the calling environment. It consequently forces the wrapper promise against the names-only proxy. R then retains that wrong answer for the typed pass. The same mistake can cause premature duplicate-set errors. This extends beyond the qualified refused-arithmetic branch repaired by #868; that closed ticket does not cover this operator-walk branch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The preserved wrapper reproductions agree with direct tidyselect/dplyr on the selected fixed key, included dimensions, and source-row membership through both nesting verbs.
- [ ] A wrapper default promise reading the active typed selection data is evaluated in the correct context even when its name is also an input column; the explicit promise variant works as well.
- [ ] Cover qualified and parenthesized operator calls supported by tidyselect as ordinary calls, for fixed keys and all five Grouping specification constructors, including local and dtplyr inspection.
- [ ] The changing-binding control no longer produces a duplicate-set refusal when the real typed selections are distinct.
- [ ] Bare tidyselect operators keep their own selection/refusal semantics and early errors; recognized nested specifications, ordinary names-only selections, and explicit all_of controls retain their documented evaluation behavior.
- [ ] Add focused public regressions and pass the package-affecting Review-ready check.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[Executed minimal reproductions, controls, cause, and investigation limits](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6570a9dec93aca220d061d9eede0205a335c367a/investigation/nesting-specification-followup-2026-10-26.md#f1-an-ordinary-wrapper-selected-the-wrong-grouping-columns). The dated note links the preserved replay scripts, their measured output, and dependency versions. No implementation is included.
title: [P2] Resolve qualified selection operators in their typed context

body:
## What to build

Resolve accepted Grouping selectors against typed selection metadata whenever their ordinary S3 or vctrs dispatch can depend on column types. Inspection, fixed-key selection, and nesting must agree with direct tidyselect rather than silently changing the requested grain.

Reproduced on main `59d55a7867ffc0255f75be32a233d9d475bcb7fb`: the input had character region values east/west and an integer amount column. A one-element integer matrix had no explicit class attribute, but ordinary `format()` dispatched to the caller's `format.matrix` method. That method selected the names of character columns from the active selection data. Direct tidyselect selected region. The same helper argument in `.by` selected no fixed key: both nesting verbs returned one two-row cell instead of two one-row cells. A rollup instead failed prematurely with “requires at least one dimension.” An explicit matrix class or an opaque wrapper around the same generic restored the correct selection.

The preflight classifier treated unclassed atomic arguments and a whitelist of base functions as sufficient evidence for a names-only answer. Ordinary S3 generics can dispatch on implicit classes even when `is.object()` is false. The measured format/unique/sort family reproduced across matrix, array, character, numeric, integer, and logical implicit classes. A related direct injected classed selector with valid vctrs cast methods also selected the wrong fixed key; its equivalent wrapped selection succeeded. Both routes belong to the same typed-selection boundary, rather than requiring two unrelated fixes.

Closed #825, #889, #924, and #975 repaired other typed-selection spellings; this is the remaining dispatch boundary. ADR 0008 governs evaluation budgets and ADR 0013 the inspected plan. No new selector syntax or source-row read is needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The implicit-class generic reproduction selects region for fixed keys and produces two correct one-row nested cells with both nesting verbs, locally and through dtplyr.
- [ ] Every applicable Grouping specification constructor resolves the dispatched selection correctly, without a premature empty-dimension or duplicate-set refusal.
- [ ] Accepted injected classed selectors respect their vctrs dispatch and agree with direct typed tidyselect and their wrapped controls.
- [ ] Preserve caller environments, the documented evaluation budget, ordinary name-only selections, existing grammar refusals, and metadata-only handling of lazy inputs. Regressions distinguish implicit dispatch from an explicit-class or opaque-wrapper control.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Evidence

[Dated investigation and runnable reproductions](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/26f5c85e8e5783403d9fbadcfa3d1d9b9604b349/investigation/2026-10-29-nest-spec-dispatch-followup/README.md#f1-ordinary-dispatch-was-mistaken-for-a-names-only-selection), recorded in PR #1005. The link is pinned to the evidence commit; the investigation did not implement the repair.
title: [P2] Respect typed dispatch when resolving Grouping selectors

body:
## What to build

Classify qualified column-selection calls by the semantics that actually execute in their captured environment. A familiar helper spelling must not cause a type-dependent caller function to run against the names-only proxy when a caller-defined namespace operator resolves that call.

On main `4c63bb917ed7ed31ff6aadf060a5eae7a32cd004`, use a frame with character `region` and integer `amount`. Capture a qualified dplyr all_of call with a constant string argument in an environment whose namespace operator instead returns a selector using peek_data and is.character to choose the character columns. Direct tidyselect on the real frame selects `region`. Inspection with the same captured selection as `.by` silently returns no fixed key, because the names-only proxy presents integer columns. Putting it in a rollup reports that at least one dimension is required, although the direct typed selection is nonempty.

The classifier recognizes the helper's namespace and spelling without accounting for the operator binding that evaluates its head. This differs from #924's foreign-package helper case and #975's pronoun-shaped subscript case. It is also independent of retaining constructor-result values: this reproduction uses an ordinary qualified helper and fails without a constructor-shaped preflight result.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Supported qualified selection calls resolved by caller namespace-operator bindings use the typed snapshot whenever their actual behavior cannot be established as names-only without running caller code.
- [ ] `.by` and selections in all five Grouping specification constructors agree with direct typed tidyselect, including the character-column reproduction.
- [ ] Cover both namespace operators, transparent head/call parentheses, and familiar helper calls nested in helper arguments where the same classification risk applies.
- [ ] Inspection and expansion retain the selected fixed partitions/dimensions, caller conditions, and existing evaluation budgets without speculative execution during classification.
- [ ] Keep genuine names-only error preflight, normal qualified helper behavior, earlier qualified/pronoun regressions, and ADR 0020's query boundary intact.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Investigation evidence

[The dated investigation](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/0ca171fdb1d231f068f95d4b6aea53794ca3cb77/investigation/expand-grouping-systematic-hunt-2026-10-29.md) records the pinned baseline, ranked hypotheses, discriminating controls, independent reproductions, bounded matrix results, and limitations. [The focused replay](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/0ca171fdb1d231f068f95d4b6aea53794ca3cb77/investigation/2026-10-29-expand-grouping-systematic-hunt/spec/reproduce-namespace-typed.R) and retained replay logs are published in PR #1053. Its `--assert` mode intentionally exits 1 on the investigated baseline; no implementation repair is included.
title: [P2] Resolve caller-defined qualified selection calls against typed metadata

body:
## What to build

`is_name_only_expr()` answers one question, and that question is the whole
specification:

> Is tidyselect's evaluation of this expression — success or failure alike —
> settled by the column names alone?

Every construct is classified by that sentence, and anything the reader cannot
answer for stays `FALSE`, so the typed snapshot resolves it. Today three
classes of expression answer `FALSE` that the sentence settles as `TRUE`, and
each of them makes preparation send the zero-row selection-proxy query before
reporting an error the names already decided. That is the ordering ADR 0005
forbids.

1. **`/`**, tidyselect's set-difference operator. Its walk descends into `/`
   exactly as it descends into `c()`, `:`, `!`, `-`, `|`, and `&`, so a `/`
   whose operands are name-only is name-only. Measured against a DuckDB
   connection, an unknown column named through `all_of()` reports locally with
   no query sent, while the same unknown column reached through
   `everything() / zzz` sends one first. Both `.grouping` and `.by` have this.

2. **The spellings tidyselect refuses outright** — `*`, `^`, `&&`, `||`. Their
   failure depends on nothing at all, so a fortiori not on column types.
   `grouping_set(g * v)` sends the query before reporting the arithmetic
   refusal. These must answer `TRUE` *without descending*: tidyselect refuses
   them before walking anything under them, so `where(is.numeric) * a` fails on
   `*` and never reaches the predicate.

3. **`one_of()`**, absent from the leaf-helper list. It reads names and nothing
   else, and `one_of(1)` is refused for its input type before any name is
   consulted. It is superseded rather than deprecated, and tidyselect keeps it.

`where()` stays `FALSE`: it is the one helper that reads column data.

## The two readers

`is_name_only_expr()` and `is_grouping_spec_predicate()` do not describe the
same grammar and must not be made to enumerate the same set. They take
different subsets of one fact — tidyselect's `walk_data_tree()` dispatch table
— because they answer different questions, and each adds what its own position
requires:

| | descends-into set | `(` | `*` `^` `&&` `\|\|` | leaf helpers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `is_name_only_expr()` | needs | **needs** — it reads the caller's expression as written, which is why `grouping_set((zzz))` already reports locally | needs, for the reason above | needs |
| `is_grouping_spec_predicate()` | needs | **must not have** — `nested_arg_expr()` has already dropped a redundant pair | needs, for its own reason: a specification nested under a refused spelling reaches it too | no use for them — it finds helpers by frame inspection |

What the two share is the descends-into set. Give that set one name both read,
and let each site add its own extras.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `is_name_only_expr()` carries a header stating the sentence above. It is
      the only AST reader in the module without one.
- [ ] A `.grouping` or `.by` selection using `/`, `*`, `^`, `&&`, `||`, or
      `one_of()` whose failure is settled by names raises before any query
      reaches the backend, for both arguments.
- [ ] The refused spellings answer without descending into their operands.
- [ ] The descends-into operator set is named once and read by both readers;
      neither list is defined as the other.
- [ ] A selection carrying a predicate still resolves against the typed
      snapshot, as it does today — including one under `/`, as in
      `everything() / where(is.numeric)`.
- [ ] A test counts backend reads rather than only asserting the diagnostic.

## Out of scope

Two shapes the same invariant settles as `TRUE` that this reader cannot
reach, each held out by a decision living elsewhere: a formula, and `.data$x`.
Both are #346.

## Blocked by

None.
title: Answer the name-only selection reader from what tidyselect settles from names alone
